title: Unique identifier linking health data to user
description: The companion app processes calorie, meal, and weight entries linked to a unique user identifier (account ID), enabling linking of all health data to a specific individual.
assumptions: User authentication is required to log entries in the app

title: Profiling through health data patterns
description: The app can analyze patterns in calorie intake, meals, and weight entries to create a detailed profile of the user's health behaviors and characteristics.
assumptions: App stores and processes historical health data

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The app requests and processes identified personal health data (calorie intake, meals, weight) that is directly associated with the user's identity.
assumptions: User is authenticated when logging entries

title: Revealing health attributes
description: Weight, calorie intake, and meal data are revealing attributes that can support identification of the data subject and expose sensitive health information.
assumptions: Health data is stored in the app

title: Sensitive health data collection
description: Weight, calorie intake, and meal data are sensitive health-related data types that should only be collected when strictly required for the app's functionality.
assumptions: Health data is necessary for app functionality

title: Potential unnecessary data analysis
description: The app may analyze, enrich, or transform health data beyond what is functionally needed for basic logging and tracking purposes.
assumptions: App may perform analytics on health data
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if app performs additional analysis beyond basic tracking

title: Limited user control over health data processing
description: Users may lack control over preferences for how their health data (calories, meals, weight) is processed, stored, or shared within the app ecosystem.
assumptions: App may have limited privacy settings
uncertainty_note: Depends on app's actual privacy controls implementation

title: Limited control over health data rectification/erasure
description: Users may lack adequate control to rectify incorrect health entries or remove personal health data that is no longer relevant.
assumptions: App may have limited data management features
uncertainty_note: Depends on app's actual data management implementation

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: Collection of detailed health data (calorie intake, meals, weight) may exceed what is minimally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: App collects more granular health data than needed
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific app functionality requirements

title: Unique identifier linking health logs to individuals
description: Health log store contains user identifiers that can link health data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) to specific individuals, enabling data correlation across the system.
assumptions: Health logs include user identification information

title: Profiling individuals through health data patterns
description: Stored health logs can be analyzed to create detailed profiles of individuals based on their health behaviors, weight trends, exercise patterns, and dietary habits.
assumptions: Health data is stored with sufficient granularity for pattern analysis

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The companion app processes and transmits identified personal health data including calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions to the datastore.
assumptions: App processes data with user identification

title: Revealing health attributes enable identification
description: Health data attributes (weight history, exercise sessions, calorie intake) are revealing and could support identification of data subjects, especially when combined with other data.
assumptions: Health attributes have identifying potential

title: Health data prevents denial of health activities
description: Stored health logs can be used as evidence to prevent individuals from denying their health-related activities, weight changes, or exercise patterns.
assumptions: Health logs are stored with attribution to users

title: Sensitive health data types collected
description: Health data including weight history, calorie intake, and exercise sessions are highly sensitive personal data types that require strict necessity justification.
assumptions: Health data is considered sensitive under privacy regulations

title: Health data retention duration
description: Health logs may be stored longer than functionally needed, creating unnecessary privacy risk through extended data retention.
assumptions: Retention policy may not be time-limited

title: User unawareness of health data processing
description: Users may not be fully aware of how their health data is being collected, processed, and stored in the health log store.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain health data processing

title: Limited control over health data rectification and erasure
description: Users may lack adequate control to rectify incorrect health data or erase health logs that are no longer relevant.
assumptions: Data subject rights implementation may be limited

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing comprehensive health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) may exceed what is functionally necessary, violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: All health data types may not be strictly necessary

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Health data may be stored longer than necessary for the stated purposes, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: Retention period may exceed functional needs

title: Health profiling through cross-session analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service analyzes calorie, weight, and exercise logs across multiple sessions to perform health-condition analysis. This enables profiling of individuals based on their health data patterns, allowing linking of data points to specific individuals through behavioral analysis.
assumptions: Health logs contain sufficient detail across sessions to enable meaningful profiling

title: Health data as quasi-identifier
description: The combination of calorie intake, weight measurements, and exercise patterns across sessions can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify individuals, especially when combined with other available data.
assumptions: Health patterns are sufficiently unique to individuals

title: Processing of highly sensitive health data
description: Health logs containing calorie, weight, and exercise data are highly sensitive personal data types. Processing this data for health-condition analysis requires careful justification and protection measures.
assumptions: Health data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable regulations

title: Health data enrichment and analysis beyond original purpose
description: The analytics service performs health-condition analysis on the health logs, which represents further treatment and analysis of personal data that may go beyond the original purpose of logging health metrics.
assumptions: Original purpose was simple logging, not health-condition analysis
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about original data collection purpose

title: Unawareness of health data analysis
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health logs are being analyzed across sessions for health-condition analysis, beyond simple storage and retrieval.
assumptions: Users may not have been informed about analytics processing

title: Lack of control over health data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack the ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their health data is processed for analytics purposes, including what analyses are performed.
assumptions: No preference mechanism exists for analytics processing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing health logs across multiple sessions for health-condition analysis may involve more personal data than strictly necessary for the stated functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: All session data is processed rather than only what's needed

title: Lawfulness concerns for health data processing
description: Health data is special category data under GDPR requiring specific lawful grounds for processing. Health-condition analysis may require explicit consent or other specific legal basis beyond general consent.
assumptions: Processing involves special category health data

title: Profiling through health analytics
description: The Health Analytics Service creates profiles of individuals by analyzing health data to generate risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags. This profiling links various data points to create a comprehensive health profile of the individual.
assumptions: The analytics service processes personal health data to derive insights about individual users

title: Revealing health attributes in analytics
description: Health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags contain revealing attributes that could support identification of the data subject, especially when combined with other data.
assumptions: The analytics insights contain attributes that could be used to identify or distinguish individuals

title: Sensitive health data disclosure
description: Health-condition risk indicators are highly sensitive personal data types that may be more sensitive than functionally required for the app's operation.
assumptions: Health risk indicators constitute sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Unnecessary data enrichment through analytics
description: The Health Analytics Service performs treatment, analysis, and enrichment of personal health data to generate insights that may not be strictly necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The analytics processing goes beyond what is minimally needed for the app's purpose

title: Unawareness of health analytics processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health data is being analyzed to generate risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags that are returned to the app.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into what analytics are being performed on their health data

title: Lack of control over health analytics preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their health data is processed for analytics and what types of insights are generated.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular consent options for different types of health analytics

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: The generation and transmission of health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags may process more personal data than is actually needed for the app's functionality.
assumptions: The analytics may include data elements beyond what is minimally necessary
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific app requirements and data elements included

title: Automated decision making on sensitive health data
description: The analytics service performs automated processing on sensitive health data to generate risk indicators and trend flags, which may raise lawfulness concerns under regulations like GDPR.
assumptions: Health data is considered sensitive personal data requiring special protections

title: Sensitive health data displayed to user
description: The app displays inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals, which are highly sensitive health data types. While the user is the intended recipient, the display of such sensitive inferred health conditions represents a significant data disclosure that should be carefully justified and controlled.
assumptions: The inferred condition indicators are considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Fine-grained health risk disclosure
description: The app displays specific inferred health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) at a granular level. This level of detail may exceed what is functionally necessary for the user to understand their health trends.
assumptions: The granularity of health risk signals could be reduced while still providing useful information

title: User unawareness of data processing implications
description: Users may not be fully aware that the app is processing and inferring sensitive health conditions from their data, and what implications this has for their privacy. The display of inferred conditions may not adequately inform users about the underlying data processing.
assumptions: Users may not understand how the app derives health risk signals from their data

title: Lack of user control over health data display
description: Users may lack control over which health indicators are displayed, how they are presented, or whether they want to see certain sensitive inferences. There may be no mechanism to customize or opt-out of displaying specific health risk signals.
assumptions: The app may not provide granular controls for users to manage what health data is displayed

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Displaying inferred health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) may process more personal data than is actually needed for the app's functionality. The necessity of displaying such sensitive inferences should be carefully evaluated.
assumptions: The display of inferred health conditions may not be strictly necessary for the app's core functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific regulatory context and whether this is considered necessary for the app's purpose

title: Automated decision making on sensitive personal data
description: The app performs automated inference of sensitive health conditions (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) and displays these to the user. This may constitute automated decision-making on sensitive personal data, which requires specific legal grounds and safeguards under regulations like GDPR.
assumptions: The inference of health conditions constitutes automated decision-making on sensitive data
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether the inference is considered automated decision-making under applicable regulations
